testing_centers.notes: Available at Pearson VUE test centers worldwide

id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. ID must match the name on the exam registration. Acceptable forms include passport, driver's license, or national ID card.
exam_rules: Open-book exam. Physical and electronic notes are permitted — building a comprehensive index is a key preparation strategy. No internet access during the exam except to pre-loaded approved materials. Proctored at Pearson VUE centers or online via ProctorU. Candidates have a 4-month window to schedule and take the exam after registration.
renewal_options: Certifications are valid for 4 years. Renewal requires 36 CPE (Continuing Professional Education) credits earned over the 4-year period, plus a $429 renewal fee. Alternatively, candidates may retake the current exam to renew.
target_audience: New InfoSec professionals with backgrounds in information systems and networking, Security professionals, managers, and administrators, Operations personnel, IT engineers and supervisors, Forensic analysts, Penetration testers, Auditors
recommended_experience: Hands-on experience in information security tasks in IT systems

prerequisites.description: Hands-on experience in information security tasks in IT systems

retake_policy.notes: Two free practice tests are included with each exam registration. Candidates have a 4-month window to take the exam after registration. Retake fees apply after the first failed attempt. Contact GIAC for specific retake waiting periods.

objectives.title: Understand the fundamental theory of access control and the role of passwords in access control management.
Demonstrate an understanding of how to secure containers and understand security features provided in MacOS.

Have a basic understanding of the concepts of cryptography, including the major types of cryptosystems, the mathematical concepts that contribute to cryptography and identify commonly used symmetric, asymmetric, and hashing cryptosystems.
Have a high-level understanding of the use, functionality, and operation of VPNs, GPG, and PKI.

domains.name: Data Loss Prevention and Mobile Device Security

objectives.title: Understand the risks and impacts of data loss, how to prevent it, and the security considerations of mobile devices.
Understand what defense in depth is, identify the key areas of security, and demonstrate the different strategies for implementing effective security within an organization.
Demonstrate how to architect a network to be monitored and controlled to resist intrusion.
Demonstrate a basic understanding of the function and uses of endpoint security devices, such as endpoint firewalls, HIDS, and HIPS.
Have a high-level understanding of the features of Group Policy and working with INF security templates.
Understand the concepts and processes associated with incident handling.
Demonstrate an understanding of the Linux operating system structure, vulnerabilities, and permissions.
Demonstrate an understanding of gaining visibility into a Linux system to be able to secure, audit, and harden the system.
Demonstrate a high-level understanding of logging importance, configuration, and SIEM assisted analysis.
Understand important attack methods and basic defensive strategies to mitigate malicious software threats and exploitations.
Demonstrate a basic understanding of the function and uses of network security devices, such as firewalls, NIDS, and NIPS.
Demonstrate an understanding of the properties and functions of network protocols and network protocol stacks.
Understand the purpose, implementation, and background of the CIS Critical Controls, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and the MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base.

domains.name: Virtualization, Cloud Security, and AI Essentials

objectives.title: Have a basic understanding of concepts of virtualization, cloud architectures, and AI fundamentals.

Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts and relationship behind reconnaissance, resource protection, risks, threats, and vulnerabilities including the creation of network maps and penetration testing techniques.
Demonstrate an understanding of web application security and common vulnerabilities including cookies, SSL, and access control.
Understand how permissions are applied in the Windows NT File System, Shared Folders, Printers, Registry Keys, and Active Directory, and how Privileges are applied.
Understand how to manage updates for a network of Windows hosts.
Understand the techniques and technologies used to audit Windows hosts and simple PowerShell scripting.
Identify the differences between types of Windows OSes and how Windows manages groups and accounts, locally and with Active Directory and Group Policy.
Understand how to take basic measures in securing Windows network services such as IPsec, IIS, and Remote Desktop Services and Microsoft Azure security features.
Have a basic understanding of the configuration and risks of wireless networks and how to secure them.
